newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope meets crown prince of Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Pope meets crown prince of Kuwait.

text.p: Pope John Paul met Kuwait's Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah on Friday for what the Vatican called cordial talks.
The private audience was the first such high-level meeting since 1969, when Kuwait became the first Gulf Arab state to establish diplomatic ties with the Vatican.
"It was a cordial courtesy visit during which (they) also had an exchange of ideas on the situation in the Middle East," Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said in a statement.

The Vatican's foreign minister Monsignor Jean-Louis Tauran visited Kuwait late last month and the Vatican said afterwards he had found a "vibrant" Roman Catholic community of some 100,000 people, mainly foreign workers.
A statement on the visit at the time compared religious freedom in Kuwait favourably with "other situations in the region".
The statement did not elaborate. Saudi Arabia, which borders Kuwait, bans public Christian worship.
The Kuwaiti news agency KUNA this month said Kuwait had approved a Vatican request to open an apostolic nunciature (embassy) in Kuwait and appoint a resident nuncio (ambassador).
A Vatican source, who asked not to be identified, said a nuncio had yet to be appointed. Vatican interests in Kuwait and other Gulf states are represented at present by the nuncio in Lebanon.
